To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the AIRS HDO/H2O ratio retrievals have a bias of 1.3% with respect to the ground-based data and that the AIRS retrievals have a precision of 3.5%.

(1) AIRS-based estimates can be used to characterize the deuterium (D/H) content of water vapor in the troposphere, and (2) the deuterium contents of water vapor in tropical and extratropical regions of the troposphere are consistent with those observed in the stratosphere, indicating that the deuterium of tropospheric water vapor is largely inherited from the stratosphere.
the AIRS-based estimates for the deuterium-to-hydrogen ratio of water vapor in the troposphere are accurate to better than 10% for all but the most arid regions, where the accuracy drops to 20-30%.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the retrieval of HDO and water vapor (H2O) from high-resolution infrared spectra measured from the Atmospheric Infrared Sounder (AIRS) on the NASA Earth Observing System Aqua spacecraft.

characterizing and evaluating the deuterium (D) content of water vapor (H2O) as retrieved from the Atmospheric Infrared Sounder (AIRS) and the Advanced Microwave Sounding Unit-A (AMSU-A) on NASA's Aqua satellite.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the AIRS-based retrievals of H2O and HDO are consistent and reliable and that the AIRS-derived estimates of the HDO/H2O ratio are accurate to better than 10% for the troposphere.
the AIRS HDO data set is of good quality and can be used with confidence for the purposes described above.
AIRS has a high sensitivity to water vapor and a high accuracy in water vapor retrievals.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the HDO and H 2O retrieval algorithm is a robust and reliable method that is capable of retrieving the tropospheric water vapor isotopic content from space.
the AIRS-based estimates for the deuterium (D) content of water vapor (H2O) in the troposphere are consistent with the values derived from in situ measurements of H2O and HDO in rainwater.
the deuterium abundance in the troposphere has increased by ~1% over the last decade.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can use the AIRS data to get a global view of the distribution of HDO in the atmosphere.
the AIRS data are of high quality, and the HDO/H2O retrievals from them have a precision that is comparable to or better than the best retrievals from the other satellite missions.
AIRS-based HDO retrievals are a promising tool for characterizing the isotopic composition of water vapor in the lower troposphere.
